assets.original_caption_tex:
Left: Overview of \MGA{}: (1) offline policy training, (2) model-based refinement,
    and (3) force-adaptive deployment with feedback.
    Right: an open-circle start-to-goal toy: (A) Gaussian-initialized refinement,
    (B) RL prior, (C) \MGA{} w/o LRC, and (D) \MGA{}.
    The prior supplies path structure. LRC reduces maximum median-path drift:
    $0.165$ (B), $0.129$ (C), $0.008$ (D).
    Arrows mark full-path maxima of distance to the realized manifold. C/D differ only in LRC.

assets.figure: Overview of the 2GO framework, LaTeX label fig:2go_overview
assets.display_caption: 2GO overview: transport selection, geometry-shaped score and exploration, CFS retraction, and deployment through a reference governor.
assets.alt: Original 2GO framework diagram showing task modulation, constraint geometry, geometric-aware generative updates, optional CFS correction, and governor-based deployment.
assets.transformation: Original standalone figure PDF rendered to 2400 px width with Poppler. Only white margins trimmed; 20 px white padding added. All original panels and labels retained.
assets.original_caption_tex:
\textbf{Overview of the 2GO framework.}
    At each reverse step, 2GO reweights model-based trajectory samples and
    selects a DDPM-, DDIM-, or flow-like transport. Task-modulated active
    constraints shape the score through $G^{-1}_k$ and filter stochasticity through
    $P_k$, with optional CFS correction; a reference governor converts the clean trajectory into executable commands. In a two-time-step foothold contact example (bottom right gray panel), the score $\hat{\mathbf S}_{k}$ guides two unconstrained foothold points, $Y_{k}^{1}$ and $Y_{k}^{2}$, which are reshaped into $\tilde{Y}_{k-1}^{1}$ and $\tilde{Y}_{k-1}^{2}$ by the $G^{-1}_k$-shaped $\hat{\mathbf S}_{k}^{G}$ and $P_k$-filtered exploration, then retracted into the support regions via CFS. The final swing trajectory is shown as a gray line.

assets.display_caption: FedGuide method visualization: policy aggregation, diffusion priors, and diffusion priors with value-baseline guidance.
assets.alt: Three original FedGuide panels compare policy-based aggregation, diffusion priors only, and priors with a value baseline in a two-client heterogeneous setting.
assets.transformation: Paper PDF page 4 rendered at 432 dpi with link annotations hidden. Figure and its three panel labels cropped; the paragraph caption and all surrounding paper text omitted. White margins trimmed and 20 px padding added.
assets.original_caption_tex:
\textbf{Method Visualization with 2 Clients Heterogeneous Settings.}
        (a) Policy aggregation averages local optima $\mathbf{x}_1^{*}, \mathbf{x}_2^{*}$ into global policy $\mathbf{x}^{(t,H)}$, away from the global optimum $\mathbf{x}^{*}$. (b) OT-MoE aggregates diffusion priors in distribution space, forming shared prior support $\bar{\pi}_{D}$ and personalized priors $\bar{\pi}_{D,1},\bar{\pi}_{D,2}$ (pink). The prior regularizer $\widehat{\mathcal R}$ (yellow) pulls local policies toward personalized prior supports. (c) FedGuide further uses the DICE value baseline (green) for policy improvement, shown as straighter policies updates and smaller endpoint dispersion ($\mathrm{Variance}\downarrow$).
